prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one universally “best” HVAC company for every Atlanta homeowner — the best choice depends on your ZIP code, budget, desired brand, timeline and whether you want a basic replacement or high‑efficiency upgrade. I can help you find a top option near you, but first here’s a short, practical plan and a few reputable names you can start with.

Quick checklist for choosing an HVAC contractor
- Verify license & insurance (ask for license number and proof of liability/workers’ comp).  
- Look for NATE‑certified technicians and a company with several years of local experience.  
- Require a Manual J load calculation (proper sizing). Don’t accept “same as old” sizing.  
- Get at least 3 written, comparable bids that list equipment model numbers, SEER rating, coil compatibility, and all labor/permit costs.  
- Confirm permits will be pulled and inspections done.  
- Ask about parts and labor warranties, and whether the labor warranty is backed by the company (not just the manufacturer).  
- Check Google/Yelp/BBB reviews for recent jobs and how the company handles problems.  
- Ask about rebates, financing, and whether they’ll dispose of the old unit.

Companies to consider (commonly recommended in Atlanta area)
- Coolray Heating & Air Conditioning — Atlanta‑based, large footprint and many local reviews.  
- Service Experts Heating & Air Conditioning — national chain with local branches and financing options.  
- One Hour Heating & Air / Benjamin Franklin (franchise) — prompt service reputation and multiple local franchises.  
- ARS/Rescue Rooter (ARS/Service Champions network) — large network that handles installations and service.

Red flags
- Pressure to sign the same day or very large down payments (>50%) before any permitting or order.  
- No written estimate or vague scope.  
- No load calc or refusal to confirm the indoor coil/tank compatibility.  
- Extremely low price compared with other bids (could be inferior equipment or missing services).

If you want, I can:
- Look up top‑rated HVAC contractors near your exact address/ZIP (share ZIP).  
- Provide a short list of questions to ask on the phone.  
- Review 2–3 written quotes and point out differences.

Which would you like next? If you share your ZIP code, budget range, and whether you want a specific brand (Carrier/Trane/Lennox/Goodman/etc.), I’ll tailor recommendations.
